MUQATIL:68:28-33/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:28-33/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:28-33/r1.claim: Their most balanced speaker, meaning fairest in speech as in 2:143, asks why they did not glorify God by saying God willing.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p310#2/r1.claim: Qatada says the brother described as the middle one was the fairest and best of them.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p480/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p480/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p480/r1.claim: The middle brother was best in conduct and most just in speech; lawlā tusabbiḥūn means “why do you not glorify God?”

TAB-FULL:v23p181/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes awsaṭuhum to mean the most just or best; Ibn ʿAbbās links “middle” with justice in 2:143.

TAB-FULL:v23p181/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the middle brother as the most just.

TAB-FULL:v23p181/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses the middle brother as the most just.

TAB-FULL:v23p181/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r4.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r4.claim: Saʿīd also says he was the most just.

TAB-FULL:v23p181/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r5.claim: Qatāda calls him the fairest in speech, quickest to fear, and best to turn back in repentance.

TAB-FULL:v23p181/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p181/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise glosses him as the most just.

TAB-FULL:v23p182/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p182/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p182/r1.claim: Mujāhid explicitly glosses tasbīḥ as making an exception; among these people, glorification meant saying “if God wills.”

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r7.claim: Their middle brother was the fairest; wasaṭ is glossed as just, as in the justly balanced community.

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r8.claim: Tasbīḥ here means making an exception to the oath by saying in shāʾ Allāh. Though tasbīḥ can mean “Glory be to God,” any magnification of God counts; the exception acknowledges that action depends on His will.

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r9.claim: Tasbīḥ linguistically means declaring God free of evil; an oath’s exception magnifies God and admits that no act occurs apart from His will.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the middle brother as the most just among them.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#3/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#3/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says that, in their time, making an exception meant saying tasbih.

NAHHAS:v5p11/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p11/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p11/r6.claim: Awsaṭuhum means the most just of them; lawlā tusabbiḥūn means 'why did you not glorify God?'.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r19.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16#2/r19.claim: Awsatuhum means their most balanced, intelligent, or excellent member.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r20.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16#2/r20.claim: Lawla tusabbihun can mean why did you not make an exception by saying if God wills.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r21.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v10p16#2/r21.claim: Abu Salih says their form of making an exception was to say Subhan Allah.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16#2/r22.claim: Other explanations ask why they did not glorify and thank God for what He gave, or ask His forgiveness for their deed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r25.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r25.claim: أوسطهم means the most just of them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r26.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r26.claim: أوسطهم means the best of them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r27.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r27.claim: أوسطهم means the most intelligent of them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r28.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r28.claim: لولا تسبحون means that they should have said an exception when they vowed to harvest in the morning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r29.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r29.claim: Making an exception is a form of glorification because it involves remembering God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r30.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r30.claim: They should have recalled God's favor and given its due from their wealth.

QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r5.claim: The middle brother was the most upright and best-spoken; he rebuked them for failing to say God willing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r3.claim: All the exegetes say the middlemost brother is the fairest and most just of them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas relates أوسط to the balanced community and the middle amount of food in 5:89 and 2:143.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r5.claim: They explain لولا تسبحون as why did you not make an exception by saying if God wills.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq says glorifying God here means making an exception, because praising Him exalts His will and admits no act occurs without it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r7.claim: Abu Salih says the exception they should have made was the phrase سبحان الله.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p105#4/r8.claim: The middle brother criticized them for leaving out an exception when they swore to harvest the orchard in the morning.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:28-34/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:28-34/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:28-34/r1.claim: The most balanced brother had asked them to glorify God, meaning to say “if God wills”; that exception counts as glorification because it exalts God.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r13.claim: They interpret awsaṭuhum as the most just in speech.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r14.claim: Other possibilities are the best and wisest, the person nearest to what is best, or the oldest among them.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r15.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r15.claim: Lā tusabbiḥūn may mean why did you not make an exception, since doing so expresses trust in God and disavowal of one's own power.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r16.speaker: أبو صالح
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r16.claim: They used subḥānallāh as their formula for making an exception.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r17.claim: Other readings urge them to glorify and remember God, thank Him for His gifts, ask His forgiveness, and return the matter to His will rather than counsel one another to deny the poor their due; the latter is Abu Muslim's explanation.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r18.claim: Another explanation is to declare God free of injustice, since He does not wrong people and does not approve their wrongdoing.

JISHUMI:v10p7034/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7034/r19.claim: The first clause may rebuke them, followed by a fresh exhortation to glorify God and return to Him.

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r5.claim: Calling one of the brothers their middlemost indicates that he was a believer who enjoined right conduct.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r2.claim: Their most balanced and intelligent brother rebuked them for not making an exception; calling it glorification recognizes that action depends on God’s will.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r3.claim: Abu Salih says their exception was the phrase ‘Glory be to God.’

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196#2/r4.claim: Other explanations are that they should glorify and thank God for His gifts, or seek His forgiveness for their deed.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r14.claim: Their الوسط brother was the fairest in speech, character, and judgment; وسط in 2:143 likewise means just and best.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r15.claim: Some interpret تسبحون as obeying and magnifying God and acting in obedience to Him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r16.speaker: مجاهد وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r16.claim: Mujahid and Abu Salih say تسبحون was their expression for making an exception.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r16.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
TABRISI:68:17-33/r16.claim: The ‘middlemost’ brother was the fairest speaker; alternatively, he was the best or wisest, or the one of middle age.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r17.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:68:17-33/r17.claim: The rebuke ‘why do you not glorify?’ means ‘why did you not make an exception?’ because exception acknowledges dependence on God's will.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r18.claim: Other interpretations say the rebuke asks why they did not worship and obey God, thank Him by giving the poor their right, acknowledge that God neither does nor approves injustice, or pray.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r1.claim: Their middle brother was the most just and virtuous among them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r2.speaker: ابن جريج والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r2.claim: The rebuke means they should have said in shāʾ Allāh while vowing to harvest in the morning.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r3.claim: Calling the exception tasbīḥ is apt because it glorifies God and recognizes that no one acts except by His will.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r4.claim: Their exception itself was the utterance subḥān Allāh.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r5.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p338#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, the brother urged them to glorify and thank God for what He had given them.

RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r1.claim: Awsat means the fairest and best among them, as discussed under the phrase 'a just community' in 2:143.

RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r2.claim: Most commentators say 'why did you not glorify?' means they should have made an exception by saying 'if God wills'; acknowledging God's will through the phrase guards against attributing a flaw to His power.

RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r3.claim: The Qurʾān indicates that they had sworn without exception, and their fairest brother had warned them against that before the disaster.

RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p79#4/r4.claim: A second view says their middle brother had urged them to repent of withholding zakat before punishment; after the disaster, they remembered his warning and immediately repented.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r1.claim: Their middle brother was the most excellent, just, and intelligent among them.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r2.claim: Mujahid and others understand “why do you not glorify?” as “why do you not make an exception by saying if God wills”; the brother had warned them, but they ignored him.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r3.claim: Abu Salih says their exception was “Glory be to God”; the brother asks why they did not praise God and thank Him for what He gave them.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas says tasbih is declaring God transcendent; Mujahid’s reading works because it denies that anything happens except by God’s will.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:28-32/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that the brother urged them to seek forgiveness and repent their corrupt intention, recalling God’s punishment of wrongdoers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:27-32/r2.claim: The most balanced among them in judgment, or the middle-aged one, had urged them to remember God and repent of their corrupt intention when they first planned it.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r1.claim: The middle brother was the most upright and best among them.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r2.claim: “Why did you not glorify God?” can mean say “if God wills,” since both expressions magnify God, or remember Him and repent of their malicious plan.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#8/r3.claim: The middle brother had earlier urged them to remember God's punishment and repent, but they disobeyed, so he rebuked them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r10.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r10.claim: Al-Naḥḥās explains this as making glorification stand for “if God wills,” since nothing occurs except by God's will.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says exception and glorification both honor God: one entrusts the matter to him, the other declares him exalted.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r12.claim: Another interpretation of “why do you not glorify?” is “why do you not seek forgiveness?”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r7.claim: أوسطهم means their best and most sensible member; he rebukes them for abandoning glorification, remembrance, and God's command to share as their father had done.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r8.claim: Their neglect of God and resolve to withhold charity brought the trial; the middle brother had previously advised and urged them to remember God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r9.speaker: مجاهد وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p243/r9.claim: Mujāhid and Abū Ṣāliḥ say their intended exception was saying “glory be to God.”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Muhammad ibn Ka‘b, al-Rabi‘, al-Dahhak, and Qatada explain their “middle” brother as the fairest and best of them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r4.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj read “why do you not glorify?” as “why did you not make an exception,” by saying “if God wills.”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says that in their time making an exception was expressed as glorification.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the exception formula as saying “if God wills.”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation is that the middle brother urged them to praise and thank God for what He had given them.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r4.claim: Their middle brother was superior in judgment, reason, age, leadership, and virtue, and had warned them that their plan was improper.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p106/r5.claim: By asking why they did not glorify God, the brother means they should have denied that their plan could override God's will; at minimum they should have said inshallah when swearing.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r10.claim: Ikrima says awsaṭ means most just wherever it occurs in the Quran.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses awsaṭuhum as the most just.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r12.speaker: السري
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r12.claim: Al-Sari says their way of making an exception in that era was glorification.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r13.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r13.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they should have said an exception when swearing to harvest early; their tasbih served as their equivalent of saying God willing.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r6.claim: Qatada calls the middle brother the most just and best in alarm and in returning to the right course.

DURR-FULL:v8p252/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p252/r9.claim: Mujahid glosses awsaṭuhum as the fairest or most just of them.

BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r2.claim: Awsaṭuhum means the most balanced in judgment, or the fairest and best of them.

BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r3.claim: Al-Kāshifī glosses the brother as best in reason, age, or sound judgment.

BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib says ‘middle’ praises moderation between two blameworthy extremes, but can describe someone between good and bad pejoratively.

BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p88#2/r5.claim: The brother reproached them for failing to glorify God and repent their corrupt plan; the story shows resolve to sin itself can bring punishment before action.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r1.claim: أوسطهم may mean their best and most balanced in judgment, reason, and opinion, or the one middle in age.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r2.claim: His rebuke asks why they did not remember God and repent of their corrupt intention; he had already urged them to do so and avert punishment.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p32#3/r3.claim: They disobeyed his earlier advice, so he now reproaches them.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r13.speaker: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, Katâde ve Dahhâk
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r13.claim: As cited by Ibn Jarir, they explain wasat in 2:143 as just; awsatuhum is its superlative, meaning the most just, discerning, good, and moderate, not middle-aged or numerically central.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r14.claim: The moderate man was a wise, just individual whose worth the group had initially failed to recognize or heed.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r15.claim: Neither extreme individualism nor collectivism is right: the individual appears in society and society stands through individuals, while both depend on God.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r16.claim: Their covenant formed by relying on God's unity, but they failed because they disregarded God's rights in their agreement and conduct.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r17.claim: Tasbīḥ here means acknowledging God's transcendence and sovereignty, rejecting injustice and domination, observing rights, and making an exception rather than acting despotically.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r18.claim: The rebuke is not merely wounded pride about being ignored; it calls them out of despair and guards against the greater sin of accusing God of injustice.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r3.claim: أوسطهم means their best and most virtuous brother; وسط can describe excellence, as in the community and prayer verses.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r4.claim: His saying lacks a conjunction because it answers their claim that they were deprived and reproaches them for disregarding his sound advice.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p86/r5.claim: The question is confirmatory, and لولا is an exhortation; تسبحون means declaring God free of disobedience by giving the poor their share.

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells of a father who always gave each rightful person a share, then five sons who planned to keep an unusually abundant harvest from Muslim poor; four agreed and the moderate brother objected.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r10.claim: The admonition to glorify God means to declare Him free of partners: their reliance on themselves and worldly causes denied God's sole will, while adding if God wills would affirm that all outcomes depend on Him.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r9.claim: Their most balanced brother reminded them that he had warned them; the meaning is fairest in judgment, not oldest in age, and his earlier words are omitted for concision.

TABATABAI:68:29-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r1.claim: Another explanation takes their failure to glorify God as failure to remember and repent for intending to harvest everything and deny the poor; this fits if exception means reserving the poor's share.

ASAD-NOTES:68:26#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:26#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:68:26#n14/r1.claim: The right-minded brother refers to the owners' failure to see that nothing happens unless God wills it.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r6.claim: Awsat can mean just or equitable, evoking balance between two extremes.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r7.claim: Tasbīḥ here means remembering God, fulfilling His due, and thanking Him for His blessing.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r2.claim: The ‘most balanced’ person is the group’s most upright and fair member; even corrupt societies may have a noble soul who repeatedly urges heedfulness and glorification of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p434/r3.claim: Tasbīḥ comprehensively includes remembering and worshipping God; the others first ignored the counsel, then recognized its truth after seeing the consequences.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r7.claim: The middle brother's call to glorify the Lord means adding the qualification 'if God wills,' as urged earlier.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r8.speaker: bazı yorumlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r8.claim: Another explanation is that the brothers should ask God's forgiveness for their intentions and conduct toward the poor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:17/r9.claim: The brothers ignored the sensible sibling's warning, recognized his correctness after seeing the destroyed garden, repented, and regretted their actions, but too late.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r13.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r13.claim: “The most moderate” can also mean the most equitable or just among the brothers.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r14.claim: The brother asks why they did not thank God and attribute their blessings to Him instead of themselves.
